results.title: Impressive.
results.text:
In agreement with all other reviews, a visit to Pashupathi Mander is a must-do when you are in Kathmandu. It shows the cleansing and cremation rituals in Hindu culture, which you are able to follow and see from the moment a dead person is brought in (they are brought in all the time as in Hindu culture, a deceased person needs to be cremated as soon as possible), cleansed, wrapped, burnt, and his/her ashes swept in the holy river. 

Apart from the cremation, there are several small temples and stupas, dedicated to Shiva, and the domain is quite large. You can easily spend 2-3 hours here. Recommended to have a good guide to explains you everything that is going on.

results.title: Famous Hindu Pilgrimage Site
results.text: Very famous and popular destination for Hindus as once in a lifetime every Hindu should go here. All major char dham darshan which is situated in the four corners of India will be completed by doing this alone temple. Lot's of small and medium size temples present in the area of the main temple. Temple has four gates as representing four dhams. This temple included in to UNESCO world heritage site.

results.title: pashupatinath temple
results.text:
Welcome to lord Shiva home...pasupatinath temple in kathmandu,nepal its a magical and very holy shiva temple where u can admire a Shiva lingam..among other unique things.
The temple is quite crowded at certain evening times..so its better to visit it early in the morning...although at 6.30 there is a aarti taking place in the banks of river bagmati right at one side of the temple.
I suggest u all visit it slowly and with enough time cause each corner is symbolic and unique..specially if u are a lord shiva devotee.
Then late in the evening...take a deep breath and enjoy the beautiful aarti and bhajans music...its recommended to stay till the end ..for about 2 h cause the place is so enchantting and magical that u wont feel like leaving.
Keep in mind that u have to go bare foot inside the temple though there is a place outside the temple you can leave your shoes....and also.. be ready to see lots of monkeys...roaming around like home.
In a word..pashupatinath temple is a must to visit in kathmandu...lord shiva will welcome you so be prepare to have his darshan.

results.title: Ridiculous price for enth
results.text:
1000 rupees per foreigner. For this you cannot enter the temples. 
On arrival when we were told this price, we jumped on TripAdvisor to see if it would be worth it. Based on the reviews we chose not to pay this ridiculous price and instead wandered around the site. We enjoyed some buildings from further away and walked down to the river to see some burning pits. 
However not long after we had walked down to the river we were chased by a security guard who demanded to see our tickets. 
Decide for yourself if you want to go, but we think 1000 rupees is a ridiculous entry price without being certain that all the money is going towards restoration.

results.title: Religious place of great importance
results.text:
This is one of the 12 Jyotirlinga which are considered the most revered of Shiva Temples, this one is outside India.
Temple is not overcrowded nor dirty, at times there will be a queue, but mostly it's difficult to offer Puja.
It's a temple complex, in which there are many, many small temples, some inhabited, some vacant.The earthquake has damaged some structures, but main temples are more or less intact.
Temple is situated on river Bagmati, and beside the temple, there is a cremation ghat.
On the other side of river there are numerous temples on the slope of a hill, some populated by Sadhus.
Great experience, not to be missed.

results.title: An insight into Hindu culture at a hefty price.
results.text:
It was a spur of the moment decision to jump into a taxi from Thamel and see Pashupatinath temple. The cab cost 350 NPR. 

There was still a lot of damage to outer buildings from the earthquakes but it is an impressive site. 

It's a complex of many temples surrounding the main temple. As a non-Hindu you cannot enter this temple but you can glimpse through the 4 main gates. 

For Hindus, cremation here means an escape from reincarnation and entry to the afterlife. However, for such a morbid, yet spiritual place, there seemed little sense of occasion. 

I would highly recommend taking up the offer of a guide when you buy the ticket for entry - and a guide certainly will offer his services!!! Entry is 1.000 NPR per person. The same was demanded by the guide, but a bit of haggling will reduce that. 

Take the chance to photograph the Sadhus. These are religious people who have renounced worldly life, yet have a price for appearing in photographs!!! The bargaining started at 2.000 NPR. 

Monkeys are in abundance at the temple but don't get too close to cause alarm. 

For those short of cash for this holy place, there are cash machines conveniently located in the complex. 

After spending a good couple of hours here, you can spend whatever money you have left in the hundreds of souvenir stalls approaching the complex. 

In summary, this was a moving experience. I've never witnessed a cremation before. Yet, religion seemed to take second place to money.

results.text: A very old shiva temple and consider as important as jyotirling. there are two queues formed. if you are in hurry, you can stand in front queue itself which is generally shorter. this queue remains on back side but barely 5 ft behind front queue but it had raised platform to do darshan so view is almost equal.

results.title: Be here for the evening aarti and see the reality of life at the cremation pyres!
results.text: Pashupatinath Temple is not only one of the most revered sites for Hindus, but also a must-visit site for everybody who want to see the Hindu funeral rites and aarti, the evening prayers at the bank of holy Bagmati River. The evening prayers are solemn and full of celebrations at the end --- the musicians and priests sing the hymns, the devotees chant along swaying their bodies to the tunes of the mantras -- and you feel like you're approaching salvation! It's so soothing and satisfying experience! Then you see the realities of life -- dead people being burnt on pyres! You'll feel like there's no need to amass wealth 'cause at the end everybody dies!

results.title: one of the best Place to visit in Kathmandu , Nepal
results.text:
In my Nepal visit, Pashupatinath was not included in my list of desired places to visit, from the net I got many negative reviews about that place. some said they took too much entry fees, some said they didn't allow to enter the Temple to non hindu visitors. but my Taxi driver told me -"if you like to do some photography, you must visit this place." 
When I enter the area I also realize it. first of all, I surprised to see that actually now the authority didn't take any entry fees from anyone.  the atmosphere is different. you can see cremation is going on, just walk through the bridge & take the stairs & it will lead you to a different zone where you can find hundreds of small old temples like buildings & many Sadhu Baba's. 
recently famous Hollywood movie Dr. Strange shows some view of this place, shooting also done in the temple premises. this place should not be missed if you travel to Kathmandu . 
P.S. due to extensive dust of cremation, Smoking Ganza by Shadu's & air pollution you should wear a mask in face.

results.title: Biggest shiva temple in Nepal
results.text: Pashupatinath is one of the biggest hindu temple in nepal, lots of festival is celebrated here like teej,shivaratri, shavan somari. Lots of people across the globe come to visit pashupatinath in shivaratri! and shivratri is said to be one of the biggest festival of lord shiva.

results.title: it is all about faith
results.text: The temple is a must visit for Hindus due to their  faith in Shiva. the temple complex is really huge . however the main temple and area around it is limited. as you enter you  gets to  see a kalaeidoscope of 'sadhus' dressed in 'bhagva' clothes and painted in an interesting manner . it is like any other Hindu temple. the holy and pure vibrations are tainted with noise, crowd, dirt  around the temples and commercialisation.

results.title: Well worth a visit but be careful of everyone wanting money
results.text: My husband and I visited the temple and ghats and enjoyed learning more about the Hindu traditions. We witnessed a couple of cremations but were horrified at all the tourists taking pictures! Some going directly up to the deceased to get a photo! One girl even taking a selfie! Please be respectful when you go! How would you like it if it was your relative getting cremated! Also be prepared to be pestered by guides wanting money and women selling jewellery who will follow you unless you are firm with them. Also the sadhus will ask for money to take their photo.

results.title: A very sacred place
results.text: A must must visit to each and every Hindu Pilgrimage or Tourist in Kathmandu. You will feel the entire journey of human life by blessings of Lord Pashupatinath.

results.title: Hindu Temple of Pashupati
results.text: The venerated Hindu Temple of Pashupatinath is well worth a visit when Kathmandu.  Just beware the fake Baba's (holy men) who encourage you to take their picture then try to charge up to $25.  If you would like a photo just be sure to set the price first which should cost no more than $100 NPR ($1 USD)

results.title: Holy Hindu Temple
results.text: The holy hindu Temple. This is a must visit place. As a foreigner you'll get to know and see the hindu culture. This is a must visit place if you are in Kathmandu.

results.title: Interesting Culture
results.text:
It was nice seeing actual cremation ceremonies performed in the temple. This was definitely one of my highlights in Kathmandu.

Guides are available upon ticket purchasing... you may hire them if you wish to know more of the history and traditions of the Nepali people.
